page: Vultr vx1-g-48c-192g is a dedicated virtual server instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor with 48 vCPUs, derived from 24 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is limited to a 1 GB NVMe SSD, which serves primarily as a boot volume, requiring external storage solutions for data-intensive applications. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark testing, the processor demonstrates strong capabilities, with single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores placing in the top 10% tier, while multi-core performance ranks in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with uncached large-block read and write speeds reaching the top 10% tier. Cryptographic and vector operations are accelerated by hardware support for AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-ni instructions. For language model workloads, the instance achieves top-tier text generation speeds across small, medium, and large models, though prompt processing speeds for larger models remain in the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a balanced allocation of dedicated compute power and memory. The primary tradeoff is the minimal 1 GB local NVMe SSD, which restricts local data storage and necessitates network-attached storage for larger databases or filesystems. Consequently, this configuration is best suited for memory-intensive general-purpose workloads, software compilation, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference where primary data resides externally.
